fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Master switch. If unchecked, the chat panel is not mounted on any Desk page.

fields.label: Iframe Base URL
fields.description: Where the chat-ui SPA loads from. Default is the bundled dist (same-origin). Override to point at a remote chat-ui (e.g. https://chat.example.com) or a dev server (http://127.0.0.1:5173) for HMR.

fields.label: Iframe Query Params
fields.description: Appended to the base URL. Default forces the sidebar layout. Add &fixture=meta for demo fixtures, etc.

fields.label: Chat Path
fields.description:
Which side of the embed orchestrates the LLM call.

* auto (default): chat-ui uses Browser-LLM if user has a custom model configured, else falls back to Backend-LLM.
* browser: always Browser-LLM. User must configure a custom model + API key in chat-ui's model picker. Keys never reach the server.
* backend: always Backend-LLM. Uses the LLM Provider + LLM Model doctypes (admin-controlled, shared keys). Custom models in chat-ui are ignored.

fields.label: MCP Endpoint
fields.description: URL the chat-ui calls to fetch tool defs and execute tools (Browser-LLM path). Read-only; rely on the default.

fields.label: LLM Proxy (Browser-LLM Path)
fields.description: When chat-ui calls cross-origin LLM endpoints (e.g. NVIDIA, OpenAI), the request is forwarded through the Frappe proxy at /api/method/lazychat_erpnext.desk_assistant.llm_proxy.handle. The allowlist below prevents using the proxy as an open relay.

fields.label: Allowed Upstream Hosts (JSON array)
fields.description: JSON list of hostnames allowed as targets for the LLM proxy. Subdomain matching: 'openrouter.ai' covers 'abc.openrouter.ai'. Add internal LLM gateways here; remove providers you don't want exposed.

fields.label: Use Legacy Vanilla-JS Widget Instead of Iframe
fields.description: When checked, the legacy claude_assistant_desk vanilla-JS panel mounts and the iframe panel is suppressed. Mutually exclusive with the iframe panel. Useful for fallback if you hit an iframe-rendering issue.

fields.label: Allow prepare_send_email Tool
fields.description: When checked, the prepare_send_email tool can stage outbound email. Defense against accidental mass-mail. site_config 'lazychat_allow_email' takes precedence if set. Cycle 10: default ON (allow-all) — defense-in-depth via /commit.

fields.label: Allow prepare_run_sql + prepare_run_python Tools
fields.description: When checked AND caller has System Manager role, the SQL and Python power tools can be staged via /commit. SELECT-only SQL enforced by regex. site_config 'lazychat_allow_dangerous_tools' takes precedence if set. Cycle 10: default ON (allow-all) — defense-in-depth via System Manager role + /commit.

fields.label: Enable Cycle 9 (auto-discovery, iterative verification, critic LLM, exemplar memory, live grounding, PEVR)
fields.description: When OFF, the assistant behaves exactly as it did pre-Cycle 9 (Cycle 8 behavior). When ON, all Cycle 9 capabilities activate, gated by Effort level. Cycle 10: default ON (allow-all).

fields.label: Allow prepare_create_email_account Tool
fields.description: When checked AND caller has System Manager role, the prepare_create_email_account tool can stage SMTP/IMAP credentials. Configuring an Email Account is meaningfully more dangerous than sending email — it can exfil mail or DOS upstream servers — so it has its own gate separate from 'Allow prepare_send_email'. site_config 'lazychat_allow_email_setup' takes precedence if set. Cycle 10: default ON (allow-all) — defense-in-depth via System Manager role + /commit.

fields.label: Enable Screenshot Preview (Playwright)
fields.description: When enabled, the chat-ui auto-captures a screenshot of new Desk Pages after Apply. Requires Playwright + Chromium installed on the bench: `./env/bin/pip install playwright && ./env/bin/playwright install chromium`.

fields.options:
Two chat paths

Browser-LLM: chat-ui (in the iframe) calls the LLM directly using a key the user pastes into chat-ui's model picker. Tools are still ERPNext tools — chat-ui calls our MCP wire endpoint to execute them. Best for single-user / power-user setups.

Backend-LLM: the existing flow. ERPNext owns the LLM key (Desk → LLM Provider) and runs the agent loop server-side. Best for org deployments with shared keys and central audit.

Both share
  • The same 38 ERPNext tools (tools.py)
  • Per-user permission scoping via frappe.has_permission
  • Server-side conversation history in 'Claude Conversation' doctype

Site_config overrides (advanced): the keys lazychat_iframe_src, lazychat_panel_enabled, lazychat_legacy_widget_enabled, lazychat_allow_email, lazychat_allow_dangerous_tools in sites/<site>/site_config.json still work and override fields here. This is for site-by-site policy.
